title: GPU CI Gating and IaC Contracts Playbook
author: Jordan Kline
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines the CI gating patterns, IaC contract tests, and runbook steps used at Redwood to ensure safe changes to GPU fleet provisioning, tenant quotas, and network egress rules. It bridges: (a) Terraform/IaC module CI, (b) runtime capacity assertions (GPU fleet and quota), (c) cloud account/network constraints, and (d) deployment runbooks for safe promotion. The goal is zero-surprise merges and automated safety checks that guard SLOs and prevent cross-tenant impact.

Contents:
1) Principles and scope
2) Pre-merge CI gates and contract tests
3) IaC test matrix and examples
4) Capacity and network invariants to assert
5) Promotion/canary pipeline & rollback policies
6) Emergency runbook (triage and rollback)
7) Ownership and oncall play
8) Appendix: sample Terraform/CI snippets and checks

Principles and scope:
- Apply to changes that affect: Terraform modules that create GPU nodes, autoscaler configs, node pool taints/labels, VPC egress/NACLs, and tenant quota resources.
- Fail fast: PRs that change contracts must fail CI if they violate invariants.
- Contracts are declarative tests (not ad-hoc scripts): modules must ship unit tests and a small integration harness.
- Minimal blast radius: every merge must have an explicit rollout plan and capacity safety net.

Pre-merge CI gates and contract tests:
- Unit IaC validation: terraform validate + tflint + custom rules.
- Module contract tests (required):
  - Schema lock: provider-compatible inputs and outputs unchanged unless a major-version bump.
  - Quota delta test: simulated change cannot increase total GPU quota for a tenant by more than configured limit without approval (default 10%).
  - Network egress ruleset test: additions that widen CIDR ranges beyond approved lists fail.
  - Immutable tags check: required tagging (cost-center, owner, env) must exist on all new resources.
- Integration smoke: ephemeral apply in ephemeral project to confirm plan/apply cycle (cost-limited).
- End-to-end gating: a PR that touches production modules must pass a staged promotion run (described below).

IaC test matrix and examples:
- Test matrix dimensions: module, cloud account (dev/stage/prod), GPU instance type family, autoscaler policy variant.
- Each module must include:
  - unit tests (mocked plan assertions)
  - terraform-compliance rules as YAML snippets for CI
  - a small acceptance test that runs terraform plan/apply in a budgeted ephemeral account and asserts post-apply resources via cloud API.

Example terraform-compliance rule (YAML):
```
# fail if new resource increases tenant_gpu_count by >10%
- name: Tenant GPU delta limit
  resource: aws_autoscaling_group
  property: desired_capacity
  operator: increase_less_than_or_equal
  value: 10 # percent
```

Capacity and network invariants to assert:
- Fleet-level invariants (checked nightly and on PRs):
  - Minimum spare GPUs across regions: 5% of total capacity or 8 GPUs, whichever is greater.
  - Preemptible/spot fallback headroom: additional 20% capacity available across spot pools.
- Per-tenant quota invariants (checked at plan time and on allocation):
  - tenant_default_limit <= 100 GPUs unless enterprise-approved.
  - quota increasing PRs must include a rollout plan and a cost estimate comment.
- Network invariants:
  - Egress CIDR allowlist per-region; any expansion requires security-review label.
  - No module may create 0.0.0.0/0 outbound rules for control-plane subnets.

Promotion / canary pipeline & rollback policies:
1) Merge to main triggers: IaC-contract CI, module unit tests, and ephemeral apply to the dev account.
2) If the PR touches prod-targeting modules, manual approval gate is required from the owning team + SRE.
3) Canary promotion (automated):
   - Deploy plan to a single canary AZ with 2-4 nodes and a synthetic traffic run (see appendix).
   - Monitor the following metrics for 30 minutes: pod evictions, scheduler latency, 95th/99th tail inference latency for representative workloads, and network error rates.
   - Success criteria: no increase >10% in tail latency, no new 5xx-rate >0.5% absolute, and no node-level OOM or kernel panic events.
4) Gradual rollout: 3 stages (10%, 50%, 100%) with automated pause points and health checks.
5) Rollback policy: automatic rollback if any stage fails health checks or if alerts fire during a 30m observation window.

Emergency runbook (triage and rollback):
- Trigger conditions: production inference error-rate spike >1% absolute, sustained latency degradation >20% P95, or capacity loss >10% cluster GPUs.
- Immediate steps (5–15 minutes):
  1. Page oncall SRE and owning infra author.
  2. Run `terraform plan` against latest state in a read-only dry-run to confirm recent changes: `make infra-plan ENV=prod MODULES=...`
  3. If a recent merge is suspected, revert the merge PR or trigger the last known-good deployment (CI job: `deploy/rollback-to/<sha>`).
  4. For capacity loss: activate emergency burst pool (pre-warmed VM pool) by toggling `emergency-burst=true` in the autoscaler feature-flag service: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://ops-api.internal/feature-flags/autoscaler -d '\{"emergency-burst":true\}'`
  5. Communicate on #infra-incident and update status page.
- Post-incident (24–72 hours): detailed RCA and a remediation PR that either fixes the underlying IaC or introduces stricter contract tests.

Ownership and oncall play:
- Module owners must be specified in module metadata file (MODULE_OWNER). The catalog CI will block merges when owner is unassigned.
- Oncall SRE owns the canary review window and the burst-pool activation permission.
- Change approvers: owning team + SRE for production-impacting changes.

CI checklist for PRs touching GPU / network modules (required):
- [ ] terraform fmt & validate pass
- [ ] tflint and policy checks pass
- [ ] contract unit tests pass (schema + quota delta + egress rules)
- [ ] ephemeral acceptance apply succeeded (logs attached)
- [ ] rollout plan and cost estimate added to PR description
- [ ] owner/approver listed and reviewer sign-off present

Operational metrics and alerts to correlate with promotions:
- Metrics to monitor: cluster_gpu_total, cluster_gpu_spare, tenancy_gpu_utilization{tenant}, autoscaler_rebalance_events, pod_eviction_rate, inference_p95_latency{model}, network_egress_errors.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - cluster_gpu_spare < min_spare_threshold for 10m -> SEV2
  - inference_p95_latency increases >20% over baseline for 15m -> SEV2
  - autoscaler_rebalance_events > 5 in 5m -> SEV3

Appendix: sample CI snippets and commands

Terraform plan step (CI):
```
export TF_VAR_environment=dev
terraform init -backend-config=backend.hcl
terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json
python tools/verify_quota_delta.py --plan plan.json --max-percent=10
```

Sample GitHub Actions fragment for contract tests:
```
name: IaC Contracts
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  lint-and-validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: terraform validate
        run: make terraform-validate
      - name: run contract tests
        run: make contract-tests
```

Terraform module metadata example (MODULE_METADATA.md):
```
name: gpu-node-pool
owner: @infra-gpu
semver: 1.2.0
required_tags: [cost-center, owner, env]
ci_contracts: [schema-lock, quota-delta, egress-allowlist]
```

Contact and escalation:
- Primary contact: infra-gpu@redwood.com (module owners auto-notify)
- Oncall SRE rotation: see /eng-infra/eng-sre/oncall-rotations (linked internally)
- For security review: tag PR with `security-review` and notify secops@redwood.com

Notes and rationale:
- Contract tests reduce surprises from drift and accidental permission/egress expansion.
- Canary + synthetic traffic is cheaper and faster than a full-region deploy and catches regressions in scheduler/ecosystem interactions.
- The playbook favors small, reversible changes and explicit approval for capacity-affecting merges.
